evals.name: add-warning-token-both-themes
evals.prompt: We need a 'warning' status style for banners and badges. Our tokens are CSS variables in src/styles/tokens.css with :root and [data-theme=dark] blocks, mapped into tailwind.config.ts. Add it.
evals.expected_output: Adds semantic warning tokens (fg/bg/border or equivalent roles) in both the light and dark blocks, maps them into the Tailwind theme, checks text/background contrast in both themes (≥4.5:1 for text), and uses them via variants of the existing Banner/Badge components rather than hardcoded values.
expectations: Defines the new tokens in both the light and the dark theme
Adds semantic role tokens (e.g. warning-fg / warning-bg / warning-border) rather than a single raw colour
Checks or reports contrast ratios for the text/background pairs in both themes
Exposes the style as a variant of existing components instead of inline colours

evals.name: audit-hardcoded-values
evals.prompt: The UI looks inconsistent across pages. Audit how well product code under src/features uses our design system and tell me what to fix first.
evals.expected_output: Runs concrete searches for raw colours, arbitrary Tailwind values, inline visual styles and hand-rolled lookalikes of shared components; reports counts and top offending files; states which rules are enforced by lint and which are not; ends with one prioritised next action (typically a lint rule with a ratchet baseline).
expectations: Reports counts from actual searches of the code rather than general impressions
Identifies hand-rolled duplicates of shared components as a category
Distinguishes rules that are mechanically enforced from those that are not
Ends with a single prioritised next action

evals.name: button-variant-api
evals.prompt: Product wants a 'destructive' button. Currently people pass className='bg-red-600 text-white' to <Button>. Fix this properly.
evals.expected_output: Adds a `danger`/`destructive` variant to the shared Button using semantic danger tokens (defined for all themes, contrast-checked, with hover/focus/disabled states), migrates existing className overrides to the variant, and adds a lint/check or ratchet against colour overrides on Button.
expectations: Adds a variant to the shared Button instead of creating a new component or keeping className overrides
The variant uses semantic tokens, not raw Tailwind palette colours
Migrates the existing className overrides to the new variant
Proposes or adds a mechanism that prevents colour overrides from creeping back

evals.name: primitive-import-order
evals.prompt: Tag.css gives .tag-warning an amber background, but warning tags render with the neutral background of the shared .chip primitive they also carry. Both are single-class selectors. src/index.tsx imports the components before './styles/primitives.css'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Explains that equal-specificity rules resolve by source order, which follows import order, and reorders imports to reset → tokens → primitives → components (or introduces @layer), instead of raising specificity on the tag.
expectations: Identifies import order (source order at equal specificity) as the cause
Moves the reset and the tokens/primitives imports ahead of the component imports, or uses @layer
Does not fix it with !important or a more specific selector on the tag
Checks other components that override the same primitives
